items.title: Formal diagram coefficient-to-observable adoption
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]], as required by the cited mathematical phase-space map.

For a specifically named finite tree calculation, adopt its selected formal
diagram coefficient as a **leading perturbative coefficient** with a stated
phenomenological reading. For QED, use the vertex and free-line conventions
of the current draft supplier
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. A particle of natural charge $q_n$ has
vertex $iq_n\gamma^a$; the electron has $q_n=-e_n$ and vertex
$-ie_n\gamma^a$. The rational fermion line is
$$ i\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}, $$
for $\mu>0$ and off-shell $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$. In Feynman gauge
the auxiliary photon line is
$$ -i\frac{h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}=i\frac{\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}. $$
For a finite matrix kernel the coefficientwise inverse in
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] is part of the formal convention and
asserts no convergence. If a time-ordered distribution is used, use the
actual free carrier specified there; that identification is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]. The displayed pole notation does not define loop
products. In the pair-production channel below the selected muon also has
model charge $-e$, and only the photon line is internal.

For declared incoming spin probabilities, sum over declared final spin
labels, and a specified formal amplitude $\mathcal A$, adopt the
cross-section coefficient map of
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. Its scattering inputs are
positive-shell energy vectors $p_i=(E_i,\mathbf p_i)$ with
$E_i=\sqrt{|\mathbf p_i|^2+\mathsf M_{i,\rm in}^2}>0$,
$\mathsf M_{i,\rm in}\ge0$, and common future-timelike total
$P=p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2$. The outgoing $k_j$ are on their specified positive
shells. Require $s=h(P,P)>(\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2)^2$ for the outgoing
rest energies and positive incoming flux $F>0$, precisely the supplier's
admissible scattering domain. In the center-of-momentum frame it
uses the invariant incoming flux $F$, the two-body measure $d\Phi_2$, and the
final-state factor $S_f=2$ for identical particles or $S_f=1$ for
distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When
this coefficient is read phenomenologically, the initial preparation,
channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No
universal error estimate for omitted terms is implied.

For the scalar examples, separately adopt the constant formal amplitudes
$\mathcal A=-\lambda$ for the quartic contact channel and $\mathcal G=G_E$
for the cubic parent decay, with the units and external normalization stated
at each use. The scalar scattering inputs lie on their stated positive
shells with a common total and the same strict threshold and positive-flux
conditions. For decay, the parent is $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$,
$\mathsf M_0>\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2$, and its two positive-shell daughters
sum to $P_0$. Their coefficient map is the one in
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. If a rate $\Gamma$ is reported as
an energy width, the convention is explicitly $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma$; it
does not supply a survival law.

The readings above do not identify a formal coefficient with an exact
continuum cross section, probability, decay rate, or measured estimate. In
particular they do not construct an interacting continuum $S$-matrix or LSZ
limit, establish convergence of a perturbation series, bound loop or
soft-radiation effects, specify beam or detector cuts, resolve threshold
resummation, or reproduce the statistical analysis of an experiment. A
comparison with observations would require the actual apparatus, sampling,
calibration, uncertainty, and radiative-inclusiveness conditions. The
reported electron magnetic-moment measurements, including the Fan et al.
report listed in the source references, remain source-reported
empirical results and are not premises of this adoption.

items.title: Formal tree scattering and scalar-decay coefficients
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the fixed Cartesian
Minkowski chart $x=(ct,\mathbf x)$, the geometric metric
$\eta=(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct algebraic contraction
$h=-\eta=(+,-,-,-)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Let $m,M\geq0$ be the
electron and muon rest energies in joules. In this chart, a future energy
four-vector is
$q=(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $E>0$; it has rest energy $\mathsf M\geq0$
when $h(q,q)=\mathsf M^2$. All four-vector components are in joules, and
$\mathbf q$ is $c$ times physical spatial momentum. Let $p_1,p_2$ be future electron
and positron energy four-vectors with rest energy $m$, and $k_1,k_2$ future
muon and antimuon energy four-vectors with rest energy $M$, satisfying
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and
$$ s=h(P,P)>4\max(m^2,M^2). $$
By [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]], choose a proper orthochronous
$h$-Lorentz matrix $\Lambda\in GL(4,\mathbb R)$, meaning
$\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the future
causal cone $C_+:=\{(E,\mathbf q):E>0,\ h((E,\mathbf q),(E,\mathbf q))\geq0\}$,
with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$.
Its boost construction supplies such a map because $P$ is future timelike.
The **center-of-momentum inertial chart** has coordinates
$x^{\rm CM}=\Lambda x$ on spacetime and corresponding four-vector components
$q^{\rm CM}=\Lambda q$; from here on, four-vector components are in that
chart, so $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$. The strict threshold makes
$\mathbf p_1$ and $\mathbf k_1$ nonzero. Define the
scattering angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ by
$$\theta:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\mathbf p_1\cdot\mathbf k_1}{|\mathbf p_1|\,|\mathbf k_1|}\right),$$
using the Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb R^3$.
Write $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0$, as in
[[def-qft-example-data]], and
$$ \beta_e=\sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{s}},\qquad \beta_\mu=\sqrt{1-\frac{4M^2}{s}}. $$
For the selected formal one-photon tree coefficient, take equal incoherent
weight $1/4$ for the four initial spin-label pairs and sum over final spin
labels. Take the selected muon model charge to be $-e$ as well. Up to an
irrelevant common phase, its amplitude is
$$ \mathcal M_{\rm tree}=\frac{g^2}{s} [\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)] [\bar u(k_1)\gamma_a v(k_2)], $$
where the brackets denote the product of the two currents. This selected
formal amplitude adopts the current draft QFT-G02 line/vertex convention;
it is not an exact amplitude of a constructed continuum theory.

Conditional on this amplitude adoption and
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], the spin-averaged squared
coefficient is
$$ \overline{|\mathcal M_{\rm tree}|^2} =g^4[3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2 +\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
The distinguishable-particle differential and total
cross-section coefficients are
$$ \frac{d\sigma_{\rm coeff}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2\beta_\mu}{4s\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2\cos^2\theta], $$
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{s}\frac{\beta_\mu}{\beta_e} [3-\beta_e^2-\beta_\mu^2+\tfrac13\beta_e^2\beta_\mu^2]. $$
For $\delta=4m^2/s\leq1/2$, the ratio of this differential coefficient to
the coefficient at $m=0$ with the same $M,s,\theta$ belongs to
$[1,1+4\delta]$. This bound is only the incoming-electron-mass effect
within the selected tree coefficient.

The on-shell equations also give
$$ P_a\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)=0,\qquad P_a\bar u(k_1)\gamma^a v(k_2)=0. $$
These are the two current contractions for this finite external-spinor
calculation; they do not assert an all-orders or loop Ward theorem.

For the separate scalar conventions of
[[post-qft-example-formal-observable-map]], let $m_s\geq0$ be a scalar rest
energy, let the incoming $r_1,r_2$ and outgoing $l_1,l_2$ lie on the
positive $m_s$-shell, meaning each $(E,\mathbf q)$ has
$E=\sqrt{|\mathbf q|^2+m_s^2}>0$, and require
$r_1+r_2=l_1+l_2=P_s$ with $s=h(P_s,P_s)>4m_s^2$.
Evaluate in a proper orthochronous center-of-momentum chart taking $P_s$
to $(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as in [F4]. Let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ be the dimensionless
constant quartic amplitude parameter. The identical-final full-sphere and
distinguishable total coefficients are respectively
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm identical} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s},\qquad \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm distinguishable} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{16\pi s}. $$
For a parent at rest of energy $\mathsf M_0>2m_s$ and a constant identical
daughter amplitude $G_E$ in joules, take the daughters on the positive
$m_s$-shell with total $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$. The rate coefficient is
$$ \Gamma_{\rm coeff} =\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \sqrt{1-\frac{4m_s^2}{\mathsf M_0^2}}\quad[\mathrm{s}^{-1}]. $$
If an energy width is named, its convention is $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma_{\rm
coeff}$ in joules. None of these coefficient statements implies an exact
survival law. The QFT-G02 postulate is a current draft carrier; its use here
retains draft status and does not imply independent acceptance.

The electron-mass estimate compares two tree coefficients only; no continuum scattering operator, loop or infrared error, threshold resummation, detector prediction, or empirical estimate is asserted.

items.title: Minimal Dirac magnetic benchmark from the adopted action
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]], as in the mathematical Dirac-matrix supplier chain. Also assume the adopted local Maxwell–Dirac action of
[[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]] with electron charge $q=-e$, $e>0$, and
rest mass $m>0$, with $q,e$ in coulombs and $m$ in kilograms. Use the
oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime
and inertial chart $x=(ct,\mathbf x)$ with
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. On
$\mathbb R^4$, the static lower potential is
$A_{{\rm SI},a}(x^0,\mathbf x)=(0,\mathbf A(\mathbf x))$: it is independent
of $x^0$, with $\phi=0$ and
$\mathbf A\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ in SI units
$\mathrm{T\,m}$. Define $\mathbf B=\nabla\times\mathbf A$ in tesla,
$$ \pi_i=-i\hbar\partial_i-qA_i,\qquad H_D=c\sum_{i=1}^3\alpha_i\pi_i+\beta mc^2, $$
as spatial differential expressions on $C^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)$.
Let $\mathcal D=C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^4)$ be their common test
domain; smooth coefficients make $\pi_i$ and $H_D$ map $\mathcal D$ into
itself. Use the Dirac matrices and adjoint of
[[def-qft-dirac-projections]] and
$$ \Sigma_i=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_i,\sigma_i),\qquad S_i=\frac{\hbar}{2}\Sigma_i. $$
The matrices $\alpha_i,\beta,\Sigma_i$ are dimensionless,
$S_i$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, $\pi_i$ has units
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $H_D$ has units joules. Let
$\psi:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ be a smooth spacetime spinor field. For a compactly supported direction
$\xi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4)$, holding $A$ fixed and
using real $\varepsilon$, define
$$\delta_\xi S_{\rm cl}:=\left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{\varepsilon=0}\hbar\int_{\mathbb R^4}\bigl(\mathcal L_{\rm nat}[\psi+\varepsilon\xi,A]-\mathcal L_{\rm nat}[\psi,A]\bigr)\,d^4x,$$
where $\mathcal L_{\rm nat}$ is the adopted density in
[[post-qft-qed-local-coupling]]. The integrand has compact support, so this
variation is finite. Assume $\delta_\xi S_{\rm cl}=0$ for every such $\xi$.
Then the compactly supported spinor-variation Euler–Lagrange equation of the
adopted action holds pointwise as a differential equation. In the natural
action normalization of [[def-qft-framework-units]], $\psi$ has engineering
length degree $-3/2$, and this equation is
$$ i\hbar\partial_t\psi=H_D\psi $$
for this pure magnetic specialization. Independently of this condition on
$\psi$, on $\mathcal D$ the spatial differential expression satisfies
$$ H_D^2=m^2c^4I_4+c^2(\boldsymbol\pi^2-q\hbar\boldsymbol\Sigma\cdot\mathbf B). $$
Writing the formal first-order square-root coefficient as
$mc^2+K/(2m)$, where
$K=\boldsymbol\pi^2-q\hbar\boldsymbol\Sigma\cdot\mathbf B$, the spin
term is $-(q/m)\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B$. Under the explicitly chosen
magnetic-energy convention
$$ H_{\rm mag}=-\boldsymbol\mu_{\rm mag}\cdot\mathbf B,\qquad \boldsymbol\mu_{\rm mag}=g_s\frac{q}{2m}\mathbf S, $$
where $H_{\rm mag}$ is an energy-valued matrix coefficient in joules,
$\boldsymbol\mu_{\rm mag}$ is a $4\times4$ matrix-valued magnetic moment
coefficient with units $\mathrm{A\,m^2}$, and $g_s$ is dimensionless.
Comparing the coefficient of
$\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B$ as a linear-form coefficient gives $g_s=2$ for
this minimal tree coefficient.
The Dirac equation is asserted only for fields satisfying the stated
stationarity condition. The square and coefficient are formal on the stated
test domain; no magnetic self-adjoint closure, full spectrum, radiative
correction, or empirical measurement is asserted.

items.physical_scope: A conditional compact-variation Dirac equation and formal minimal magnetic coefficient for a smooth static pure magnetic background. The result is the minimal/tree Pauli coefficient only: it proves no self-adjoint magnetic closure, full spectrum, Landau-level construction, radiative correction, or empirical equality.

items.title: Massless formal annihilation angular contrast
items.statement:
Use the massless $m=M=0$ case of the formal tree theorem
[[pthm-qft-example-formal-scattering-decay]], including its stated
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis, with $s>0$. Explicitly take
incoming $p_1,p_2$ and outgoing $k_1,k_2$ on the positive massless shell,
so each $(E,\mathbf q)$ has $E=|\mathbf q|>0$, with
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and $h(P,P)=s>0$. Use the theorem's proper
orthochronous center-of-momentum chart $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$;
$\theta$ is the Euclidean angle between the nonzero spatial parts of
$\Lambda p_1$ and $\Lambda k_1$. The differential
coefficient at $\theta=0$ is twice its value at $\theta=\pi/2$; integrating
over the full sphere gives
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}=\frac{4\pi\alpha^2(\hbar c)^2}{3s}. $$
All three quantities are formal coefficients in the adopted map, not event
counts or exact measured cross sections.

items.title: Scalar symmetry factor and conditional lifetime model
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ [[def-countable-choice]], as
required by the cited phase-space map and the Borel restriction of Lebesgue
measure.

Let $s>0$, dimensionless $\lambda\in\mathbb R$, parent energy
$\mathsf M_0>0$, and
$G_E\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$ in joules. For scattering, take the incoming $p_1,p_2$ and outgoing $k_1,k_2$
on the positive massless scalar shell, each $(E,\mathbf q)$ having
$E=|\mathbf q|>0$, with common total
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$, $h(P,P)=s>0$, and evaluate the coefficient in a
proper orthochronous center-of-momentum chart
$\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as in the phase-space supplier.
For decay, take massless positive-shell daughters summing to the rest parent
$P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$. With these data the identical
final-state quartic total coefficient is
$$ \sigma_{\rm coeff}^{\rm identical} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s}, $$
and the distinguishable-final coefficient is twice this value. The
identical-daughter decay-rate coefficient is
$$ \Gamma_{\rm coeff}=\frac{|G_E|^2}{32\pi\hbar\mathsf M_0} \quad[\mathrm{s}^{-1}]. $$
Set $\Gamma:=\Gamma_{\rm coeff}>0$. For the lifetime calculation only, let
$(\Xi,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)$ be a probability space in the sense of
[[def-probability-measure]]: $\mathcal F$ is a sigma-algebra on $\Xi$, and
$\mathbb P$ is a countably additive measure with $\mathbb P(\Xi)=1$. Let
$\mathcal B([0,\infty))$ be the sigma-algebra generated by sets
$U\cap[0,\infty)$ for open $U\subseteq\mathbb R$, as in
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]. Let
$T:\Xi\to[0,\infty)$ be a parent lifetime measured in seconds and measurable
in the explicit sense that $T^{-1}(B)\in\mathcal F$ for every
$B\in\mathcal B([0,\infty))$. Define its law by
$\mu_T(B):=\mathbb P(T^{-1}(B))$ on those Borel sets. Let $\ell$ denote
one-dimensional Lebesgue measure from
[[def-lebesgue-measure-and-the-lebesgue-sigma-algebra]], restricted to
$\mathcal B([0,\infty))$; this restriction is a measure by
[[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]] under the stated Countable Choice
assumption. Separately assume the exponential lifetime model, defined by
$$\mu_T(B)=\int_B\Gamma e^{-\Gamma t}\,d\ell(t)\quad\text{for every }B\in\mathcal B([0,\infty)).$$
It gives $P_{\rm surv}(t):=\mathbb P(T^{-1}((t,\infty)))=e^{-\Gamma t}$ for
$t\geq0$. Define the
mean lifetime as $\mathbb E[T]:=\int_{[0,\infty)}t\,d\mu_T(t)$, and define
the half-life $t_{1/2}$ by $P_{\rm surv}(t_{1/2})=1/2$. Then the mean
lifetime is $1/\Gamma$ and the half-life is $\ln 2/\Gamma$. The exponential
law is not a consequence of the formal coefficient calculation.

items.physical_scope: A massless-daughter scalar formal coefficient example. It explicitly adds an exponential survival model before deriving a mean and half-life; the formal rate coefficient by itself implies neither time law.

items.title: Minimal Dirac spin and orbital coefficient comparison
items.statement:
Take $q=-e$ with $e>0$, $m>0$, and a constant field
$\mathbf B=B_0\hat z$ with $B_0>0$. It is realized by the smooth SI
potential
$$ \mathbf A(x,y,z)=\frac{B_0}{2}(-y,x,0),\qquad \phi=0, $$
for which $\nabla\times\mathbf A=B_0\hat z$, where $\hat z=(0,0,1)$.
Under the Countable Choice and adopted-action hypotheses of
[[pthm-qft-example-dirac-magnetic-benchmark]], the formal spin term is
$-(q/m)\mathbf S\cdot\mathbf B=(e/m)S_zB_0$. Since
$\Sigma_z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1,-1)$, its two spin eigenvalue
coefficients are
$$ \Delta E_{\uparrow,\downarrow}=\pm\frac{e\hbar B_0}{2m},\qquad \Delta E_{\rm gap}=\frac{e\hbar B_0}{m}. $$
Define the comparison orbital coefficient by
$\omega_{c,\rm orb}:=eB_0/m$ and
$\nu_{c,\rm orb}:=\omega_{c,\rm orb}/(2\pi)$. The cyclic coefficient
frequency of the spin gap is
$$ \nu_{s,\rm coeff}:=\frac{\Delta E_{\rm gap}}{2\pi\hbar} =\frac{eB_0}{2\pi m}=\nu_{c,\rm orb}. $$
This is a comparison of formal minimal coefficients. It is not the full
Landau spectrum, a radiative correction, a prediction of zero measured
anomaly, or a laboratory measurement.
